newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait shares slip from record levels.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait shares slip from record levels.

text.p: The Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) index eased 3.3 percent in the past two days with trading values and volumes slipping after a record week.
The index on Sunday closed at 2,260.1 points, a drop of 76.5 points from Wednesday's pre-weekend close and 94.6 points from last Sunday's record high. The KSE operates Saturday to Wednesday.

Some analysts, including KSE Director-General Hisham al-Oteibi, had expected a market correction, while some parliamentarians voiced concern on Saturday of the risk of a possible crash, similar to the 1982 collapse of Kuwait's unregulated Souq al-Manakh bourse.
"Normally after a rise there are correction moves," Oteibi told Reuters last week. "They are always a possibility and are expected, but not a crash...No way, impossible."
Kuwait's cabinet on Sunday discussed market developments in a meeting attended by Oteibi, the Central Bank governor and the director-general of the state Kuwait Investment Authority.
"The Cabinet reviewed an assessment report on activity on the KSE in the past quarter," an official statement said.
On Sunday some 211 million shares worth 58.4 million dinars ($192.1 million) were traded, compared with last week's record daily average of 345 million shares worth 99.4 million dinars.
On Monday 445 million shares worth 125.8 million dinars changed hands.
The index, which rose some 40 percent in 1996, after a similar gain in 1995, is 18.6 percent higher than at the start of 1997.
Trading on the KSE is open only to nationals of Oman, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Qatar. Kuwait's foreign residents can trade through mutual funds.
Sixty-six firms with a market capitalisation of about $24 billion are listed on the Kuwait bourse.
